learning_objective: 🎯 Step out of the textbook and become a real sociologist by learning how to conduct practical research, surveys, and field observations!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Sociologists must observe society objectively (as it is, without bias), but human emotions and subjective perspectives (how people feel) are also critical data.
Collecting data from a large number of people using structured questionnaires to find statistical patterns (e.g., the national Census).
In-depth conversations with individuals. They can be structured (strict list of questions) or unstructured (free-flowing conversation to uncover deeper feelings).
A method where the researcher lives with and participates in the daily life of the group they are studying to truly understand their culture from the inside.

fun_activity.title: 📝 The Mini-Survey
fun_activity.instructions: Create a 5-question survey about 'Screen Time Habits' or 'Favorite Street Food' and ask 10 of your friends to fill it out. Analyze the results to find the most popular answer!

exam_tips: 📌 Be clear on the difference between Quantitative methods (Surveys/Stats) and Qualitative methods (Interviews/Observation).
📌 Always mention the importance of 'informed consent' and ethics when conducting sociological research.
📌 Remember that formulating a clear 'Research Question' is the most important first step of any project.
quick_recap: ⭐ Participant observation was famously used by social anthropologists studying tribal cultures.
⭐ A good questionnaire avoids 'leading questions' that force a person into answering a certain way.
⭐ Doing sociology practically helps unlearn the biases we hold as 'common sense'.
